signals.source_text: Vairis and a cluster of desert Giants had been working for three months on the structure—layering sandstone blocks in a step-pyramid formation that was supposed to amplify vrill-resonance through geometric progression.
That shift propagated upward through fifty vertical feet of carefully stacked architecture, each layer magnifying the instability of the one below.

Nephoretti dove for cover behind surviving structures or simply threw themselves flat against sand and hoped the debris wouldn't reach them.
And where the pyramid had stood, now only rubble remained, scattered across two hundred yards of desert beach.
But one of them—the tall sandstone-textured Giant who had first approached Olythae's art—knelt and began reshaping the debris.
